brief: Goldman's Prime desk reports a third straight week of net equity selling (6 of last 7), driven by heavy single-stock shorting, as SPX fell 8.6% to below 7,000 and NDX fell 10.4%, the worst week since March 2020, amid an AI-trade unwind. Vol is in extreme stress: VIX above 35, the desk's panic index at 9.8/10 (readings above 9.5 have historically preceded relief), NDX over 20% off highs and technically oversold. CTAs are net short $19bn of equity length after selling $57bn over the month and are modeled to keep selling; HF leverage has fallen to multi-year lows. The desk draws a 4Q2018 analogy: High-Beta Cyclicals (+12% YTD) have so far outperformed as the market rotated out of AI rather than pricing outright downside, but could underperform sharply if growth fears (not inflation) take over, as happened in 2018. Sector dispersion: Financials hit hardest, Energy bought; Healthcare hit by policy headlines; Industrials/Materials showed wide earnings-driven stock dispersion; Energy desk stays cautious on oversupply risk into 2027.
